meanings.note: Location. Core Russian adv meaning 'here' in everyday speech.
emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').
Neuter главное, used as a noun. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('main, most important').

examples.trans: The main thing is, don't worry.
The most important thing is the people.

meanings.en: to value, to appreciate, to esteem
meanings.note: Takes accusative. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to value, to appreciate', paired with 'оценить'.

examples.text: Город высоко ценит вас и вашего мужа.
examples.trans: The city values you and your husband highly.

examples.text: Слушай, Лёля, я очень ценю, что ты приехала.
examples.trans: Listen, Lyolya, I really appreciate that you came.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'that', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.trans: Our restaurant is located right here.

examples.text: Мы теперь работаем в этом отеле.
examples.trans: We now work in this hotel.
How does a hotel restaurant differ?

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Present есть; у меня есть = I have. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to be; there is'.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: mostly in set phrases: иметь совесть, иметь право = to have the right; everyday 'I have' is у меня есть

examples.trans: You have the right to remain silent.

examples.text: Нина, имей совесть! Я вчера ради вас всё сделал.
examples.trans: Nina, have a heart! Yesterday I did everything for you.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: иметь в виду = to mean, to have in mind
иметь в виду = to mean, to have in mind

examples.text: Из окна красивый вид на парк.
examples.trans: There is a nice view of the park from the window.

examples.text: Что вы имеете в виду, Клавдия Викторовна?
examples.trans: What do you mean, Klavdia Viktorovna?

meanings.note: наш, наша, наше, наши; agrees with the noun

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Dining establishment. Borrowed from French 'restaurant' (from 'restaurer', to restore strength with rich broth); entered Russian in the early 19th century.

examples.trans: They called from the Italian restaurant.
In the evening they went to a restaurant.

examples.text: Кстати, звонили из итальянского ресторана. Дарят папе романтический ужин на двоих.
examples.trans: By the way, they called from the Italian restaurant. They're giving Dad a romantic dinner for two.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'friend' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

examples.text: Это Паша, мой заместитель. Это Ваня, друг моего детства.
examples.trans: This is Pasha, my deputy. This is Vanya, my childhood friend.

meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Question word and conjunction. Core Russian adv meaning 'when' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: When I grow up, I'll be the mayor.

meanings.note: Core Russian adv meaning 'then, later, afterwards' in everyday speech.

+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.
the person who likes is in the dative: мне нравится = I like it

examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: At that time. Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.
Core Russian adv meaning 'then, back then' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Я тебе тогда сказал: ты меня ещё поцелуешь.
examples.trans: I told you back then: you'll kiss me one day.

meanings.note: давай + 1st person plural or infinitive
давай + 1st person plural or infinitive

meanings.note: Прямо так = just like that. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: She's pretty. But that's not your wife! I've seen your wife.
